subject: Re: Performance SLO and VPC/on-prem network qualification — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO and VPC/on-prem network qualification — post-call recap

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about Acme's real-time document ingestion use case. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get the performance qualification moving: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- P95 end-to-end inference latency requirement: <= 200 ms for non-streaming requests (batch size typical), and streaming token latency target: initial token <= 120 ms and per-token tail latency <= 50 ms.
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,000 req/s peak (bursty), with expected steady-state ~250 req/s.
- Concurrent model contexts: up to 200 concurrent streams.
- Token sizes: typical prompt 400–800 tokens, responses 50–300 tokens.
- SLO objective: 99.9% availability and p95 latency targets above during business hours.

Network / deployment constraints you mentioned:
- Private deployment in Acme VPC (preferred) or on-prem with site-to-site VPN as fallback.
- Egress must come from a fixed set of IPs for firewall rules.
- Internal latency budget between your inference clients and model-hosting subnets should be < 25 ms to meet p95 targets.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) Acme to run an initial network traceroute + ping/iperf from the client subnet to the planned Redwood ingress (we'll provide endpoints) and share results (Sam).
2) Acme to confirm preferred connectivity option: VPC peering / PrivateLink (recommended) vs. site-to-site VPN. If VPN, provide tunnel details and NAT/egress IPs (Priya).
3) Redwood (Jordan + Connor) to provide a performance test harness + reference traffic profile (QPS, payloads) and a short runbook for streaming validation. We'll also share a small sample Dockerized load generator.
4) Schedule a 60-minute network deep-dive with your infra team next week to validate MTU, TCP windowing, and TLS termination expectations (all).

Attachments: I attached a simple private deployment diagram and our network checklist to guide the traceroutes and firewall rules.

If that aligns with your expectations, I'll drop the endpoints and the test harness by EOD and propose a couple of slots for the network call.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: acme-network-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO and VPC/on-prem network qualification — post-call recap

Thanks, Marissa — this is perfect. A couple quick clarifications from our infra/security side: 

- Do you require TLS termination at Redwood's edge, or can we terminate TLS at our load balancer and use mTLS to the Redwood ingress?
- For peering: we typically prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink for lower jitter. If we do site-to-site VPN, will your test harness account for the additional 10–20 ms tunnel overhead in the latency targets?
- Regarding egress IPs: we need a stable list of IPs to add to our firewall; can you provide both IPv4 and IPv6 ranges if available?

I'll start the traceroute/iperf tests this afternoon and share results. Also looping in our network engineer (cc'd).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sam

Marissa / Connor,

Quick internal note after Sam's reply — action items to prep before the network call: 

1) Create and upload the test harness (load-generator + sample payloads) to the shared drive. Include both streaming (chunked HTTP, SSE) and non-streaming REST profiles.
2) Provide a short doc outlining TLS options we support for Private (edge TLS, mTLS to ingress, in-cluster TLS) and recommended configurations for minimal latency.
3) Prepare a small checklist for MTU (1500 vs 9000), TCP tuning hints (window size), and recommended keepalive settings for long-lived streams.
4) Draft the fixed egress IP list (v4) and confirm whether IPv6 is supported for this deployment.

I'll own (1) and (3). Marissa, can you take (2) and confirm egress IPs with infra? I'll schedule the 60-minute deep-dive for Wed/Thu next week and invite Acme's network folks.

Thanks — Jordan

Sam / Priya — thanks for the quick reply. 

We can support either option (edge TLS or mTLS into our ingress). For the lowest jitter and most predictable latency we recommend PrivateLink/VPC peering where available — peering avoids tunnel overhead and simplifies IP whitelisting. If you go the VPN route we'll include an allowance in our test expectations for the tunnel overhead and ask you to validate under the same tunnel conditions.

I've uploaded the initial test harness and checklist to the shared drive (link below) and attached the same files to this message. Jordan will walk through TCP/MTU tuning during the deep-dive. Proposed network call times: Wed Apr 24 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu Apr 25 14:00–15:00 PT — please confirm which works for your infra team.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example

Next deliverables from Redwood (by EOD Tue):
- test-harness.zip (load generator + profiles)
- tls-options.md (supported TLS modes and recommendation)
- egress_ips_v4.txt (list of fixed IPv4 egress addresses)

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
